sanskrit: punaś cāsṛjad ugrāṇi śaravarṣāṇi pāṇḍavaḥ amarṣī balavān kruddho didhakṣann iva pāvakaḥ
english: Once more the mighty Pāṇḍava, brooking no insult and ablaze with wrath, let loose his fierce torrents of arrows, like a fire bent on consuming all.

sanskrit: tasya tāny ādade karṇaḥ sarvāṇy astrāṇy abhītavat yudhyataḥ pāṇḍuputrasya sūtaputro 'stramāyayā
english: But Karṇa, the charioteer's son, fearlessly received all those weapons of the warring son of Pāṇḍu, neutralizing them by the wizardry of his own missiles.

sanskrit: tasyeṣudhī dhanurjyāṃ ca bāṇaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ raśmīn yoktrāṇi cāśvānāṃ karṇo vaikartano 'cchinat
english: With his smooth-jointed shafts Karṇa Vaikartana cut apart Bhīma's quivers, his bowstring, and the reins and traces of his horses.

sanskrit: athāsyāśvān punar hatvā tribhir vivyādha sārathim so 'vaplutya drutaṃ sūto yuyudhānarathaṃ yayau
english: Then, having slain his horses, with three arrows he pierced his charioteer, who leapt down and fled swiftly to the chariot of Yuyudhāna.

sanskrit: utsmayann iva bhīmasya kruddhaḥ kālānalaprabhaḥ dhvajaṃ ciccheda rādheyaḥ patākāś ca nyapātayat
english: As though smiling, the wrathful Rādheya, radiant as the fire of doom, severed Bhīma's banner and brought down his pennons.

sanskrit: sa vidhanvā mahārāja rathaśaktiṃ parāmṛśat tām avāsṛjad āvidhya kruddhaḥ karṇarathaṃ prati
english: Bereft of his bow, O great king, Bhīma seized the lance kept in his car, and whirling it in his fury, hurled it at Karṇa's chariot.

sanskrit: tām ādhirathir āyastaḥ śaktiṃ hemapariṣkṛtām āpatantīṃ maholkābhāṃ ciccheda daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But the son of Adhiratha, straining hard, with ten arrows cut to pieces that gold-adorned lance as it came on, blazing like a great meteor.

sanskrit: sāpatad daśadhā rājan nikṛttā karṇasāyakaiḥ asyataḥ sūtaputrasya mitrārthe citrayodhinaḥ
english: Cleft into ten pieces by the shafts of Karṇa, it fell, O king — shafts loosed by that charioteer's son, fighter of wondrous skill, in the cause of his friend.

sanskrit: sa carmādatta kaunteyo jātarūpapariṣkṛtam khaḍgaṃ cānyataraprepsur mṛtyor agre jayasya vā tad asya sahasā karṇo vyadhamat prahasann iva
english: Then the son of Kuntī took up his shield and his gold-mounted sword, seeking now one of two ends — death or victory; but Karṇa, as if laughing, shattered them both in an instant.

sanskrit: sa vicarmā mahārāja virathaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ asiṃ prāsṛjad āvidhya tvaran karṇarathaṃ prati
english: Stripped of his shield, O great king, his chariot gone, swooning with rage, Bhīma whirled his sword and flung it in haste at Karṇa's car.

sanskrit: sa dhanuḥ sūtaputrasya chittvā jyāṃ ca susaṃśitaḥ apatad bhuvi nistriṃśaś cyutaḥ sarpa ivāmbarāt
english: That keen-edged blade, having cut through the charioteer's son's bow and its string, fell to the earth like a serpent dropping from the sky.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasyādhirathir anyad ādatta kārmukam śatrughnaṃ samare kruddho dṛḍhajyaṃ vegavattaram
english: Then, laughing, the son of Adhiratha, enraged, took up in the battle another bow — slayer of foes, firm-stringed, and swifter still.

sanskrit: sa bhīmasenaḥ kupito balavān satyavikramaḥ vihāyasaṃ prākramad vai karṇasya vyathayan manaḥ
english: Then mighty Bhīmasena, true in valor and roused to wrath, sprang up into the sky, troubling the heart of Karṇa.

sanskrit: tasya tac caritaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃgrāme vijayaiṣiṇaḥ layam āsthāya rādheyo bhīmasenam avañcayat
english: Seeing this feat of him who sought victory in the fray, Rādheya, biding his moment, foiled Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: tam adṛṣṭvā rathopasthe nilīnaṃ vyathitendriyam dhvajam asya samāsādya tasthau sa dharaṇītale
english: Not finding him — for Bhīma, his senses shaken, had crouched hidden upon a chariot floor — Karṇa came up to his banner and stood there upon the ground.

sanskrit: tad asya kuravaḥ sarve cāraṇāś cābhyapūjayan yad iyeṣa rathāt karṇaṃ hantuṃ tārkṣya ivoragam
english: For this all the Kurus and the celestial bards honored Bhīma — that from his car he had sought to slay Karṇa, as Tārkṣya seizes a serpent.

sanskrit: sa chinnadhanvā virathaḥ svadharmam anupālayan svarathaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā yuddhāyaiva vyavasthitaḥ
english: His bow shorn away and his chariot lost, yet keeping to the duty of his order, Bhīma set his own car at his back and stood firm, still ready to fight.

sanskrit: tad vihatyāsya rādheyas tata enaṃ samabhyayāt saṃrabdhaḥ pāṇḍavaṃ saṃkhye yuddhāya samupasthitam
english: Having broken his resolve, Rādheya then bore down upon the Pāṇḍava, furious, as he stood there in the battle, ready for combat.

sanskrit: tau sametau mahāraṅge spardhamānau mahābalau jīmūtāv iva gharmānte garjamānau nabhastale
english: The two mighty warriors met in that great arena, contending, roaring like two thunderclouds in the heavens at the close of the hot season.

sanskrit: tayor āsīt saṃprahāraḥ kruddhayor narasiṃhayoḥ amṛṣyamāṇayoḥ saṃkhye devadānavayor iva
english: Fierce was the encounter of those two wrathful lions among men, neither brooking the other in the fray, like that of a god and a demon.

sanskrit: kṣīṇaśastras tu kaunteyaḥ karṇena samabhidrutaḥ dṛṣṭvārjunahatān nāgān patitān parvatopamān rathamārgavighātārthaṃ vyāyudhaḥ praviveśa ha
english: His weapons spent and hard pressed by Karṇa, the son of Kuntī, seeing elephants slain by Arjuna lying fallen like mountains, and being weaponless, entered in among them to bar the path of Karṇa's chariot.

sanskrit: hastināṃ vrajam āsādya rathadurgaṃ praviśya ca pāṇḍavo jīvitākāṅkṣī rādheyaṃ nābhyahārayat
english: Reaching the herd of elephants and entering that rampart against chariots, the Pāṇḍava, desiring to keep his life, did not press his attack upon Rādheya.

sanskrit: vyavasthānam athākāṅkṣan dhanaṃjayaśarair hatam udyamya kuñjaraṃ pārthas tasthau parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: Then, seeking a foothold, the son of Pṛthā, conqueror of hostile cities, heaved up an elephant slain by Dhanaṃjaya's shafts and stood his ground.

sanskrit: tam asya viśikhaiḥ karṇo vyadhamat kuñjaraṃ punaḥ hastyaṅgāny atha karṇāya prāhiṇot pāṇḍavo nadan
english: Karṇa with his arrows blasted that elephant of his to pieces; then the Pāṇḍava, roaring, flung the elephant's limbs at Karṇa.

sanskrit: cakrāṇy aśvāṃs tathā vāhān yad yat paśyati bhūtale tat tad ādāya cikṣepa kruddhaḥ karṇāya pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Chariot-wheels, horses, draught-beasts — whatever he saw upon the ground, that the enraged Pāṇḍava caught up and hurled at Karṇa.

sanskrit: tad asya sarvaṃ ciccheda kṣiptaṃ kṣiptaṃ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ vyāyudhaṃ nāvadhīc cainaṃ karṇaḥ kuntyā vacaḥ smaran
english: All this, as fast as it was flung, Karṇa cut apart with his sharp shafts; yet, weaponless though Bhīma was, Karṇa did not slay him, remembering the word he had given to Kuntī.

sanskrit: dhanuṣo 'greṇa taṃ karṇas tv abhidrutya parāmṛśat utsmayann iva rādheyo bhīmasenam uvāca ha
english: Rushing upon him, Karṇa touched him with the tip of his bow, and Rādheya, as if smiling, spoke thus to Bhīmasena:

sanskrit: punaḥ punas tūbaraka mūḍha audariketi ca akṛtāstraka mā yotsīr bāla saṃgrāmakātara
english: "Again and again, you beardless dolt, you slave of your belly, you who have learned no weapon-craft — do not fight, you child, you coward in battle!"

sanskrit: yatra bhojyaṃ bahuvidhaṃ bhakṣyaṃ peyaṃ ca pāṇḍava tatra tvaṃ durmate yogyo na yuddheṣu kathaṃ cana
english: "Where there is food of many kinds, things to chew and things to drink, O Pāṇḍava — there, foolish one, you belong; never anywhere in battle."

sanskrit: munir bhūtvātha vā bhīma phalān yad dhi sudurmate vanāya vraja kaunteya na tvaṃ yuddhaviśāradaḥ
english: "Become an ascetic, Bhīma, and live on fruits, O most witless one; go to the forest, son of Kuntī — you are no master of warfare."

sanskrit: phalamūlāśane yuktas tvaṃ tathātithibhojane na tvāṃ śastrasamudyoge yogyaṃ manye vṛkodara
english: "You are fit for feeding on fruits and roots and for entertaining guests; I do not think you fit for the wielding of weapons, Vṛkodara."

sanskrit: puṣpamūlaphalāhāro vrateṣu niyameṣu ca ucitas tvaṃ vane bhīma na tvaṃ yuddhaviśāradaḥ
english: "With flowers, roots, and fruits for your fare, amid vows and observances, you suit the forest, Bhīma — you are no master of warfare."

sanskrit: kva yuddhaṃ kva munitvaṃ ca vanaṃ gaccha vṛkodara na tvaṃ yuddhocitas tāta vanavāsaratir bhava
english: "What has war to do with the life of a sage? Go to the forest, Vṛkodara; you are not made for battle, my friend — take your delight in dwelling in the woods."

sanskrit: sūdān bhṛtyajanān dāsāṃs tvaṃ gṛhe tvarayan bhṛśam yogyas tāḍayituṃ krodhād bhojanārthaṃ vṛkodara
english: "Chivvying cooks and servants and slaves in the house, you are fit to thrash them in your rage for the sake of a meal, Vṛkodara."

sanskrit: kaumāre yāni cāpy āsann apriyāṇi viśāṃ pate pūrvavṛttāni cāpy enaṃ rūkṣāṇy aśrāvayad bhṛśam
english: And whatever galling things had passed in their boyhood, O lord of peoples, those old harsh deeds too he made him hear over and over.

sanskrit: athainaṃ tatra saṃlīnam aspṛśad dhanuṣā punaḥ prahasaṃś ca punar vākyaṃ bhīmam āha vṛṣas tadā
english: Then again, as Bhīma cowered there, the Bull of men touched him with his bow, and laughing, addressed him once more:

sanskrit: yoddhavyam āviśānyatra na yoddhavyaṃ tu mādṛśaiḥ mādṛśair yudhyamānānām etac cānyac ca vidyate
english: "If you must fight, fall upon someone else; you should not fight with such as me. Those who battle men of my kind meet with this and worse."

sanskrit: gaccha vā yatra tau kṛṣṇau tau tvā rakṣiṣyato raṇe gṛhaṃ vā gaccha kaunteya kiṃ te yuddhena bālaka
english: "Or go to where the two Kṛṣṇas are — they will guard you in the fight; or go home, son of Kuntī. What have you, child, to do with war?"

sanskrit: evaṃ taṃ virathaṃ kṛtvā karṇo rājan vyakatthata pramukhe vṛṣṇisiṃhasya pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: Having thus stripped him of his chariot, Karṇa, O king, vaunted over him in the very presence of the Lion of the Vṛṣṇis and of the great-souled son of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: tato rājañ śilādhautāñ śarāñ śākhāmṛgadhvajaḥ prāhiṇot sūtaputrāya keśavena pracoditaḥ
english: Then, O king, the hero whose banner bore the monkey, urged on by Keśava, sent stone-whetted arrows against the charioteer's son.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārthabhujotsṛṣṭāḥ śarāḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ gāṇḍīvaprabhavāḥ karṇaṃ haṃsāḥ krauñcam ivāviśan
english: Then the gold-decked shafts loosed from the arm of Pṛthā's son, sprung from Gāṇḍīva, fell upon Karṇa as swans descend on the Krauñca mountain.

sanskrit: sa bhujaṃgair ivāyastair gāṇḍīvapreṣitaiḥ śaraiḥ bhīmasenād apāsedhat sūtaputraṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: With arrows shot from Gāṇḍīva, taut like outstretched serpents, Dhanaṃjaya drove the charioteer's son back from Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: sa chinnadhanvā bhīmena dhanaṃjayaśarāhataḥ karṇo bhīmād apāyāsīd rathena mahatā drutam
english: His bow shorn by Bhīma and himself struck by Dhanaṃjaya's shafts, Karṇa swiftly withdrew from Bhīma upon his great chariot.

sanskrit: bhīmo 'pi sātyaker vāhaṃ samāruhya nararṣabhaḥ anvayād bhrātaraṃ saṃkhye pāṇḍavaṃ savyasācinam
english: And Bhīma too, that bull among men, mounting a horse of Sātyaki's, followed in the battle his brother, the Pāṇḍava Savyasācin.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇaṃ samuddiśya tvaramāṇo dhanaṃjayaḥ nārācaṃ krodhatāmrākṣaḥ praiṣīn mṛtyum ivāntakaḥ
english: Then, taking aim at Karṇa, Dhanaṃjaya in haste, his eyes red with wrath, sent forth an iron shaft as Death sends out the destroyer.

sanskrit: sa garutmān ivākāśe prārthayan bhujagottamam nārāco 'bhyapatat karṇaṃ tūrṇaṃ gāṇḍīvacoditaḥ
english: Like Garutmān in the sky stooping upon the foremost of serpents, that iron shaft, sped from Gāṇḍīva, flew swiftly down upon Karṇa.

sanskrit: tam antarikṣe nārācaṃ drauṇiś ciccheda patriṇā dhanaṃjayabhayāt karṇam ujjihīrṣur mahārathaḥ
english: That iron shaft Droṇa's son cut in mid-air with a feathered arrow, the great chariot-warrior seeking to deliver Karṇa from the peril of Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: tato drauṇiṃ catuḥṣaṣṭyā vivyādha kupito 'rjunaḥ śilīmukhair mahārāja mā gās tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Then the wrathful Arjuna pierced Droṇa's son with sixty-four stone-honed arrows, O great king, crying, "Do not flee — stand fast!"

sanskrit: sa tu mattagajākīrṇam anīkaṃ rathasaṃkulam tūrṇam abhyāviśad drauṇir dhanaṃjayaśarārditaḥ
english: But Droṇa's son, sore beset by Dhanaṃjaya's shafts, swiftly plunged into the host thronged with rutting elephants and crowded with chariots.

sanskrit: tataḥ suvarṇapṛṣṭhānāṃ dhanuṣāṃ kūjatāṃ raṇe śabdaṃ gāṇḍīvaghoṣeṇa kaunteyo 'bhyabhavad balī
english: Then with the roar of Gāṇḍīva the mighty son of Kuntī overwhelmed the twanging din of the gold-backed bows that sang upon the field.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayas tathā yāntaṃ pṛṣṭhato drauṇim abhyayāt nātidīrgham ivādhvānaṃ śaraiḥ saṃtrāsayan balam
english: Dhanaṃjaya, as Droṇa's son thus fled, pursued him from behind for no great distance, terrifying the host with his arrows.

sanskrit: vidārya dehān nārācair naravāraṇavājinām kaṅkabarhiṇavāsobhir balaṃ vyadhamad arjunaḥ
english: Rending with his iron shafts the bodies of men, elephants, and horses, Arjuna scattered the host with arrows fledged in the plumes of heron and peacock.

sanskrit: tad balaṃ bharataśreṣṭha savājidvipamānavam pākaśāsanir āyastaḥ pārthaḥ saṃnijaghāna ha
english: That host, O best of the Bharatas, with its horses, elephants, and men, the son of Pṛthā — offspring of the Chastiser of Pāka — straining hard, smote down utterly.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ahany ahani me dīptaṃ yaśaḥ patati saṃjaya hatā me bahavo yodhā manye kālasya paryayam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Day after day my blazing glory falls away, Saṃjaya; many of my warriors are slain. I deem this the turning of Time.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayas tu saṃkruddhaḥ praviṣṭo māmakaṃ balam rakṣitaṃ droṇakarṇābhyām apraveśyaṃ surair api
english: Dhanaṃjaya in his fury has entered my host — a host guarded by Droṇa and Karṇa, one that not even the gods could penetrate —

sanskrit: tābhyām ūrjitavīryābhyām āpyāyitaparākramaḥ sahitaḥ kṛṣṇabhīmābhyāṃ śinīnām ṛṣabheṇa ca
english: his prowess swelled by those two of mighty valor, joined with Kṛṣṇa and Bhīma and with the Bull of the Śinis.

sanskrit: tadā prabhṛti mā śoko dahaty agnir ivāśayam grastān hi pratipaśyāmi bhūmipālān sasaindhavān
english: From that hour grief burns me like a fire within my heart, for I see the lords of earth, the Saindhava among them, already in its grip.

sanskrit: apriyaṃ sumahat kṛtvā sindhurājaḥ kirīṭinaḥ cakṣurviṣayam āpannaḥ kathaṃ mucyeta jīvitaḥ
english: Having done so grievous a wrong to the Diademed one, how can the king of the Sindhus, once come within his sight, escape with his life?

sanskrit: anumānāc ca paśyāmi nāsti saṃjaya saindhavaḥ yuddhaṃ tu tad yathā vṛttaṃ tan mamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ
english: By reasoning I see, Saṃjaya, that the Saindhava is no more. Tell me, then, as I ask, how that battle came to pass.

sanskrit: yac ca vikṣobhya mahatīṃ senāṃ saṃloḍya cāsakṛt ekaḥ praviṣṭaḥ saṃkruddho nalinīm iva kuñjaraḥ
english: And tell of him who, having shaken and churned that great army again and again, entered it alone in his wrath, as an elephant breaks into a lotus-pool.

sanskrit: tasya vṛṣṇipravīrasya brūhi yuddhaṃ yathātatham dhanaṃjayārthe yat tasya kuśalo hy asi saṃjaya
english: Tell me truly of the battle of that Vṛṣṇi hero, of what he did for Dhanaṃjaya's sake — for in this you are skilled, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tathā tu vaikartanapīḍitaṃ taṃ; bhīmaṃ prayāntaṃ puruṣapravīram samīkṣya rājan naravīramadhye; śinipravīro 'nuyayau rathena
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing Bhīma, that foremost of men, thus harried by Vaikartana and now moving away amid the heroes, O king, the hero of the Śinis followed after him in his chariot.

sanskrit: nadan yathā vajradharas tapānte; jvalan yathā jaladānte ca sūryaḥ nighnann amitrān dhanuṣā dṛḍhena; saṃkampayaṃs tava putrasya senām
english: Roaring like the Wielder of the thunderbolt at the end of the heats, blazing like the sun at the close of the rains, he smote his foes with his firm bow, making your son's army tremble.

sanskrit: taṃ yāntam aśvai rajataprakāśair; āyodhane naravīraṃ carantam nāśaknuvan vārayituṃ tvadīyāḥ; sarve rathā bhārata mādhavāgryam
english: As that hero among men ranged the field, borne by horses bright as silver, all your chariot-warriors, O Bhārata, could not turn back that foremost of the Mādhavas.

sanskrit: amarṣapūrṇas tv anivṛttayodhī; śarāsanī kāñcanavarmadhārī alambusaḥ sātyakiṃ mādhavāgryam; avārayad rājavaro 'bhipatya
english: But Alambusa, that best of kings, filled with indignation, fighting without retreat, bow in hand and clad in golden mail, rushed upon Sātyaki, the foremost of the Mādhavas, and stayed him.

sanskrit: tayor abhūd bhārata saṃprahāras; tathāgato naiva babhūva kaś cit praikṣanta evāhavaśobhinau tau; yodhās tvadīyāś ca pare ca sarve
english: Such an encounter arose between them, Bhārata, as had never been before; the warriors, both yours and the foes', all stood merely gazing at the two, splendid in battle.

sanskrit: avidhyad enaṃ daśabhiḥ pṛṣatkair; alambuso rājavaraḥ prasahya anāgatān eva tu tān pṛṣatkāṃś; ciccheda bāṇaiḥ śinipuṃgavo 'pi
english: Alambusa, that best of kings, with main force pierced him with ten shafts; but the Bull of the Śinis cut down those shafts with his own arrows even before they reached him.

sanskrit: punaḥ sa bāṇais tribhir agnikalpair; ākarṇapūrṇair niśitaiḥ supuṅkhaiḥ vivyādha dehāvaraṇaṃ vidārya; te sātyaker āviviśuḥ śarīram
english: Again, with three keen, well-feathered arrows like fire, drawn to the ear, he pierced him; rending his armor, they sank into Sātyaki's body.

sanskrit: taiḥ kāyam asyāgnyanilaprabhāvair; vidārya bāṇair aparair jvaladbhiḥ ājaghnivāṃs tān rajataprakāśān; aśvāṃś caturbhiś caturaḥ prasahya
english: Tearing his body with those blazing arrows, swift as fire and wind, with yet others Sātyaki forcibly struck down his four horses, bright as silver, with four shafts.

sanskrit: tathā tu tenābhihatas tarasvī; naptā śineś cakradharaprabhāvaḥ alambusasyottamavegavadbhir; hayāṃś caturbhir nijaghāna bāṇaiḥ
english: Thus struck by him, the swift grandson of Śini, in might like the Wielder of the discus, slew Alambusa's horses with four arrows of surpassing speed.

sanskrit: athāsya sūtasya śiro nikṛtya; bhallena kālānalasaṃnibhena sakuṇḍalaṃ pūrṇaśaśiprakāśaṃ; bhrājiṣṇu vaktraṃ nicakarta dehāt
english: Then, with a broad-headed shaft like the fire of doom, he struck off the head of his charioteer, and severed from the trunk that radiant face, earringed and bright as the full moon.

sanskrit: nihatya taṃ pārthivaputrapautraṃ; saṃkhye madhūnām ṛṣabhaḥ pramāthī tato 'nvayād arjunam eva vīraḥ; sainyāni rājaṃs tava saṃnivārya
english: Having slain in battle that son and grandson of a king, the crushing Bull of the Madhus then, O king, the hero turned back your troops and followed after Arjuna alone.

sanskrit: anvāgataṃ vṛṣṇivaraṃ samīkṣya; tathārimadhye parivartamānam ghnantaṃ kurūṇām iṣubhir balāni; punaḥ punar vāyur ivābhrapūgān
english: Seeing that best of the Vṛṣṇis come on, wheeling thus amid the foe and smiting the Kuru forces with his arrows, again and again, as the wind scatters masses of cloud —

sanskrit: tato 'vahan saindhavāḥ sādhu dāntā; gokṣīrakundenduhimaprakāśāḥ suvarṇajālāvatatāḥ sadaśvā; yato yataḥ kāmayate nṛsiṃhaḥ
english: his Sindhu-bred steeds, well broken, bright as cow's milk, jasmine, the moon, and snow, decked with nets of gold, those noble horses bore him wherever the lion among men desired.

sanskrit: athātmajās te sahitābhipetur; anye ca yodhās tvaritās tvadīyāḥ kṛtvā mukhaṃ bhārata yodhamukhyaṃ; duḥśāsanaṃ tvatsutam ājamīḍha
english: Then your sons together, and other warriors of yours, rushed upon him in haste, O scion of Ajamīḍha, putting at their head, O Bhārata, your son Duḥśāsana, foremost of fighters.

sanskrit: te sarvataḥ saṃparivārya saṃkhye; śaineyam ājaghnur anīkasāhāḥ sa cāpi tān pravaraḥ sātvatānāṃ; nyavārayad bāṇajālena vīraḥ
english: Hemming in the son of Śini on every side in the battle, those who could withstand whole armies smote him; but that hero, the foremost of the Sātvatas, held them off with a net of arrows.

sanskrit: nivārya tāṃs tūrṇam amitraghātī; naptā śineḥ patribhir agnikalpaiḥ duḥśāsanasyāpi jaghāna vāhān; udyamya bāṇāsanam ājamīḍha
english: Swiftly driving them off with feathered shafts like fire, the slayer of foes, the grandson of Śini, raising his bow, struck down even the horses of Duḥśāsana, O scion of Ajamīḍha.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tam udyataṃ mahābāhuṃ duḥśāsanarathaṃ prati tvaritaṃ tvaraṇīyeṣu dhanaṃjayahitaiṣiṇam
english: Saṃjaya said: As the mighty-armed one rose up against the chariot of Duḥśāsana, swift in the hour that called for swiftness and seeking Dhanaṃjaya's welfare —

sanskrit: trigartānāṃ maheṣvāsāḥ suvarṇavikṛtadhvajāḥ senāsamudram āviṣṭam ānartaṃ paryavārayan
english: the great archers of the Trigartas, with banners wrought of gold, surrounded the Ānarta hero who had plunged into the ocean of their host.

sanskrit: athainaṃ rathavaṃśena sarvataḥ saṃnivārya te avākirañ śaravrātaiḥ kruddhāḥ paramadhanvinaḥ
english: Then, hemming him in on all sides with their array of chariots, those wrathful, peerless bowmen overwhelmed him with showers of arrows.
